# S1. Reproducibility and software

All analyses were conducted in R. Meta-analytic models were fitted using `metafor`, and score-based sign-flipping inference was performed using `flipmeta`. Random-number seeds were fixed for all simulation and resampling procedures.

The source code used to generate the simulations, empirical application, figures, and tables is available in the accompanying repository. The manuscript and supplementary materials were generated directly from Quarto source files.


::: {#tbl-software .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Main software versions used to reproduce the analyses.'}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Software   |Version |
|:----------|:-------|
|R          |4.6.1   |
|Quarto     |1.8.21  |
|metafor    |5.0.1   |
|flipmeta   |0.0.1   |
|flipscores |1.3.2   |
|dplyr      |1.2.1   |

The supplementary materials were rendered on Linux 7.1.1-76070101-generic x86_64 from Git commit d93f327d0c0031e92d4fc144388a3b2794b4c9bf.

# S2. Computational comparison with permutation testing

The main manuscript notes that score sign flipping avoids repeated refitting of the complete meta-regression model. We illustrate the practical computational difference using a mixed-effects meta-regression with 100 independent studies and three predictors.

Both procedures used 1,000 resampling transformations. The benchmark is intended only as an illustration; computation times depend on the model, hardware, software versions, and number of resampling transformations.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

:::



::: {#tbl-computational-benchmark .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Illustrative computation times for 1,000 resampling transformations.'}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Procedure            | Time (seconds) |
|:--------------------|:--------------:|
|metafor::permutest() |      9.79      |
|flipmeta             |      0.14      |


:::
:::


In this example, `metafor::permutest()` required approximately 9.8 seconds, compared with 0.14 seconds for `flipmeta`.

# S3. Additional simulation results

The main manuscript reports simulation results averaged over study sample size and moderator correlation. Here we show the corresponding results separately across these conditions.

## S3.1 Type I error


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Empirical Type I error rates across study sample sizes and moderator correlations. The horizontal dotted line indicates the nominal significance level of .05. Wald is omitted for readability because it showed substantial Type I error inflation in several conditions. Baseline heterogeneity, scale heterogeneity, and moderator correlation are denoted by τ², ζ, and ρ, respectively.](supplementary_files/figure-pdf/fig-type1-detailed-1.pdf){#fig-type1-detailed fig-align='center'}
:::
:::


The disaggregated results show the conditions underlying the averages reported in the main manuscript and allow calibration to be inspected across study sample size and moderator correlation.

## S3.2 Statistical power

As in the main manuscript, power is shown only for method-condition combinations that adequately controlled Type I error under the corresponding null condition.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Empirical power across study sample sizes and moderator correlations. Results are shown only for method-condition combinations that adequately controlled Type I error under the corresponding null condition. Baseline heterogeneity, scale heterogeneity, and moderator correlation are denoted by τ², ζ, and ρ, respectively.](supplementary_files/figure-pdf/fig-power-detailed-1.pdf){#fig-power-detailed fig-align='center'}
:::
:::


These results complement the aggregated power results reported in the main manuscript.

# S4. CBT depression specification curve

The specification curve below displays the complete set of unique analyses, ordered by their pooled effect estimate. “Non-discriminating” indicates that multiple nominal levels of a decision produced the same final analysis after conditioning on the other decisions.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Specification curve for the CBT depression multiverse ($S = 336$ unique analyses). The upper panel shows pooled Hedges' $g$ estimates, classified by unadjusted and step-down max-$T$ significance. The lower panel shows the analytical decisions defining each analysis; 'Non-discriminating' indicates that multiple levels produced the same final model.](supplementary_files/figure-pdf/fig-specification-curve-1.pdf){#fig-specification-curve fig-align='center'}
